problem: Mobile manipulation pipelines choose the base pose for a learned manipulation policy by geometric reachability, which ignores the policy's sensitivity to its initial pose. The only policy-aware alternative, Mobi-pi, needs the policy's training data, a pre-built 3DGS scene reconstruction and about 270 s of inference per query, so it is impractical and unsuited to dynamic scenes.
motivation: Modern learned manipulation policies (BC-Transformer, DP, ACT, pi0) often fail from kinematically feasible base poses because the observation falls outside their training distribution. This gap between navigation end pose and manipulation start pose hurts overall success, especially in sequential tasks. The paper therefore asks for a fast, black-box, policy-aware base-pose predictor that needs little data.
key_idea: Learn a GMM distribution over policy-preferred base poses from a single egocentric RGB point cloud, supervised by successful policy rollouts and trained with viewpoint augmentation, which re-renders each collected scene from many viewpoints under the same pose label.
insight: Policy preference is a property of the local scene structure, so the same label can be reused across viewpoints, which gives strong data efficiency and viewpoint robustness. The ablation (Fig. ablation) shows viewpoint augmentation contributes most, with success rising with the number of augmented views M and saturating near M=300, while encoder choice and pretraining matter little. Learning from rollouts rather than training-data similarity lets N2M sometimes beat the oracle, since the policy's preferred poses need not match its demonstration distribution.
method: Input and encoder: an egocentric RGB point cloud from the onboard RGB-D camera, downsampled to 8192 points and encoded by a fine-tuned Point-BERT into a latent vector.

GMM head: an MLP predicts weights, means and covariances of a K-component GMM over SE(2) base poses (plus torso height in the real robot). K=2 for Close Drawer, otherwise K=1. It is trained by negative log-likelihood plus regularizers (weight entropy, inter-mode distance, mode entropy).
Rollout supervision: place the robot at varied poses in the task area, run the black-box policy, and record poses of successful rollouts together with a stitched local scene reconstruction S.

Viewpoint augmentation: sample M (about 300) collision-free viewpoints in the task area from which the object is visible, render the point cloud from each, and label all with the same preferred pose. Extra augmentation: random Z rotation and translation within 1 m.
Inference: one forward pass, then sample a collision-free pose from the GMM using a 2D occupancy map from the point cloud, and navigate there with a simple base planner before running the policy.

setting.backbone: Point-BERT + MLP GMM head (fine-tuned from pretrained); downstream manipulation policies BC-Transformer, Diffusion Policy, ACT, pi0
setting.training_data: 20-70 successful policy rollouts per setting in simulation (5-70 in the applicability study; 3-12 in the real Lamp Retrieval task), augmented with about 300 rendered viewpoints per rollout
setting.observation: egocentric RGB point cloud from an RGB-D camera (wrist camera in sim with GT depth, ZED 2i on the head in the real world)
setting.action_space: predicted base pose distribution in SE(2) (x, y, θ), plus torso height h on the real robot; then a simple differential-drive base planner
setting.privileged: Sim uses ground-truth depth and robot location for perfect point-cloud reconstruction. Rollout success labels are needed at training time. Otherwise none at test time.

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 independent experiments x 50 inference trials, Diffusion Policy
numbers.backbone: Point-BERT + GMM head; policy Diffusion Policy (Mobi-pi checkpoint)
numbers.extra: 20 successful rollouts, viewpoint augmentation; human data time 20.7 min, training 3.4 h
numbers.evidence: Table 1: N2M 0.55±0.07 (S_DP), inference 0.07±0.03 s; Reachability 0.16, Mobi-pi 0.24, Oracle 0.93

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 independent experiments x 50 inference trials, BC Transformer
numbers.backbone: Point-BERT + GMM head; policy BC Transformer

numbers_note: Most results are given only in figures (success rates across tasks, policies, data amounts, generalization, real-world Lamp Retrieval, sequential task, ablations), so exact values are unavailable. The only tabulated numbers are the Close Drawer benchmark in Table 1, reported as fractions (0.55, 0.56) in the paper.
results: On the RoboCasa Close Drawer benchmark, N2M reaches 0.55 (DP) and 0.56 (BC) success versus Mobi-pi 0.24/0.09 and Reachability 0.16/0.15, with 0.07 s inference against 273.5 s for Mobi-pi. Figures show N2M near or above the oracle across tasks and policies, matching it with about 10 rollouts on PnPCounterToCab, and improving both real-world Lamp Retrieval and a sequential task over Reachability and Human-intuition baselines.
limitations: Sensitive to small objects, far distances (out of the augmented viewpoint range) and noisy sensors; needs high-quality point clouds.
Requires collecting labeled policy rollouts per policy and task, and cannot fix a policy whose preferred-pose region is intrinsically narrow.
Sim uses ground-truth depth and teleports the base; several real-world tasks are qualitative only, with rule-based labels and no trained policy.
